Dear Midori,

Thank you very much for inviting the children to visit you during the summer vacation. They are extremely excited and looking forward to it. Regarding the places they would like to visit, which you asked about, they said they wanted to go to 「Disneyland」 and 「KidZania」. I feel bad asking this, but would you be able to take them there? I know this will be a great deal of trouble for you, Midori, but I would sincerely appreciate your help.

Sincerely,

default.p.II-1.vietnamese:
Most robots in Japan have machine-like forms and are working in factories. There are even robots that manufacture robots. Some robots replace people by repeatedly performing the same task, while others can do delicate work that humans cannot. Robots that perform dangerous tasks that people cannot do are especially useful.

Recently, humanoid robots that can walk, explain things at reception desks, or entertain people by playing musical instruments have also been developed. However, creating a robot that can do everything a human can do must be extremely difficult. Robots have only just reached the point where they can walk, so movements similar to those of humans are completely impossible for them. The appearance of such a robot is probably still just a dream. Nevertheless, technologies developed through this research are helping people in other fields. For example, walking-robot technology is being applied to devices that help people with difficulty walking move around independently.

Robots that do housework, such as cleaning and watching over a home, have also been developed. Although they cannot perform all aspects of caring for people, robots are being used for tasks such as moving someone from a bed to a wheelchair. In the future, robots of this kind may become the most necessary. I hope their development will be promoted so that people’s lives can become richer and more convenient.

One thing that surprises foreigners visiting Japan is the high-tech toilet. I have also heard that some people are confused because they do not know how to use one when they see it for the first time. The type of toilet they are talking about is called a warm-water washing toilet, a toilet that can wash the user's bottom. There are also models that dry the bottom, automatically open the lid, or flush automatically.

This type of toilet was first sold in Japan in 1980. Because it is convenient and hygienic, the household penetration rate exceeded 70% within 30 years. Moreover, it has continued to improve and develop from the early models, which only had a washing function. Today, it is widely used not only in homes but also in hotels, shopping centers, restaurants, and other places, giving foreigners many opportunities to see it. As a result, some foreigners reportedly become fascinated with Japanese-style toilets and buy them to take home.

(Note 1) Warm-water washing: washing with hot or warm water.

(Note 2) Penetration rate: an indicator showing what percentage of people use something.

default.p.II-11.vietnamese:
Choosing a gift to take when visiting someone who is ill can be difficult. Depending on the person’s condition, some foods may not be suitable as gifts. If the patient is feeling bored, some light reading might cheer them up. However, the most common gift is probably still flowers. In Japan, though, there are some things to keep in mind when bringing flowers to visit someone who is ill. This is because certain flowers should not be brought to patients.

First, there are potted plants. Naturally, a plant grown in a pot has roots. This suggests “being confined to bed,” meaning that the illness will last a long time. Among cut flowers, cyclamens are beautiful. However, the name sounds like 「死苦」, meaning death and suffering. Thoughts of death and suffering can worsen the recipient’s mood. Chrysanthemums are also unsuitable because they are widely used at funerals in Japan.

Camellias, or tsubaki, are also disliked. It is said that the sight of the entire flower falling at once resembles a head being severed. In addition, strongly scented flowers such as lilies can make patients feel tired, so they should not be brought. This may be similar in other countries as well.

Furthermore, when visiting someone who cannot move independently, it may be wise to check whether someone can change the water for the flowers.

In Japan, although the population is declining, the amount of CO2 emitted by households has not decreased at all. Many households are switching to energy-saving products such as air conditioners and refrigerators. Compared with models from 10 years ago, modern air conditioners use only about one-third as much electricity. Other products have also become increasingly energy-efficient, so electricity consumption per household has decreased considerably. Nevertheless, overall CO2 emissions have increased compared with the past. This is because the number of households is increasing. For example, if a family of four that once lived together separates into two households, two of every electrical appliance will be needed. Furthermore, even when people live together, the fact that each person owns a separate television, computer, phone, and so on is another contributing factor. Therefore, unless our lifestyles change, CO2 emissions from households will continue to increase.

(Note 1) Carbon dioxide: CO2. A substance produced when things are burned...

(Note 2) Energy conservation: An abbreviation of 省エネルギー. It means not using energy wastefully.

Since I am such a serious member of the "nagara-zoku" that I cannot even turn off the television while working, I was delighted to hear this good news. Researchers had two women perform various tasks to investigate how their brain activity changed. The results showed that when doing complicated tasks such as cooking, it is best to combine them with a simple activity such as listening to music. Recently, in Japan's cities, whenever there is heavy rain, water immediately floods the area. In the past, rainwater would seep into the ground, but nowadays roads are paved with asphalt (Note 1), a material that does not allow water to pass through (Note 2). As a result, rainwater flows directly into drainage systems (Note 3). Eventually, the excessive amount of water causes flooding. Therefore, when constructing large buildings, people have called for cooperation in installing large rainwater storage tanks (Note 4) in basements. However, this alone will not solve the problem. In the future, it is thought that large rainwater storage tanks should be built underground in parks and plazas, while efforts should also be made to develop road surfaces that allow water to seep through.

（Note 1）Asphalt: A black material used to harden roads and make their surfaces more durable.

（Note 2）Paving: The act of hardening a surface with concrete or asphalt to increase its load-bearing capacity.

（Note 3）Wastewater: Dirty water flowing out of kitchens, bathrooms, factories, and so on.

（Note 4）Rainwater storage tank: A container used to store rainwater.

Recently, free services have been increasing. How can a free business model continue to exist? Free products and services often have limitations. Take free video websites, for example: they offer both free and paid videos. If the video you want to watch is a paid one, you have no choice but to pay. On gaming websites, the games are free, but they use a system in which you cannot continue playing smoothly unless you buy various items. In the end, people make purchases. Those who pay are the ones supporting and maintaining the free system. There are also cases in which a free service remains viable because it receives advertising revenue from other parties. The other day, I was introduced to a free insurance plan. Along with it came an application form for a paid insurance plan. They expected customers to sign up for both. In the end, the premiums for the free insurance plan would be paid by those who purchased the paid plan. I think we must not forget that someone is always paying on our behalf.

These days, buying prepared food to take home, known as nakashoku, is becoming much more popular than eating out. Eating out means going to a restaurant, while nakashoku means buying food that someone else has prepared and taking it home instead of cooking it yourself. It is much cheaper than eating out. For people who live alone, cooking even a little is troublesome. In addition, prepared food tastes better than it did in the past, so they apparently do not want to go to the trouble of cooking. As a result, prepared-food counters in supermarkets and department stores are crowded everywhere. They also sell nostalgic dishes like the ones mothers used to make, often called “home-cooked flavors.” Even dishes from expensive restaurants that would be difficult to visit can be bought easily, although they are not cheap. Since all one has to do is buy the food, arrange it on the table, and eat it immediately, it is extremely convenient and valuable for busy people.

However, in the past, even when families made the same dish, each household had its own distinctive flavor. Nowadays, everywhere seems to have become similar in taste. The flavors of individual families, traditionally passed down from parents to children, are gradually disappearing. It feels somewhat sad and regrettable.

(Note) Osouzai: side dishes.

There is a way to get rid of an itch completely. It is said that when the brain receives a lot of information at the same time, it becomes confused. At that point, the brain is said to choose the more important information. What is most important to human beings? Apparently, the order is: 1 Pain, 2 Heat, 3 Cold, ... Information necessary to protect one’s life is given priority.

In terms of importance, the sensation of itching is apparently ranked quite low. Therefore, when we are itchy, if we provide information of a higher level, the brain devotes all its effort to transmitting that information and forgets to transmit the information that we are itching. From this, we can understand why the childhood habit of pressing a fingernail into a mosquito bite to make it hurt was actually effective. That said, when I have an itch, I do not like having to do something painful or endure heat. Therefore, it is best to apply something cold to the body when it itches. Apparently, it does not matter where you cool it. Since the itchy area is giving off heat, cooling that area is good. However, it is said that if you cool the area too much, it will itch even more when you remove the cold object. Therefore, it can be said that the best approach is to cool the itchy area first and then cool other parts of the body.

default.p.II-7.vietnamese:
Transportation in Japan is expensive but very convenient. Except for buses, all forms of transportation run on time. In addition, trains run so frequently in major cities that you do not even need to check the timetable before going to the station. However, because many different trains pass through the same stations, getting on the wrong one can cause a great deal of trouble. There are also often several ways to reach your destination station. In such cases, you should check carefully which train will get you there fastest or most cheaply.

The Tokyo subway is very complicated, and even Japanese people get lost. You need to be especially careful when changing lines. If you change trains inside the station, there is no problem, but if you have to leave the station once before changing trains, you must exit through the orange ticket gate marked 「のりつぎ」. If you exit through another ticket gate, your ticket will be swallowed there, and you will have to buy another one. Since subway stations provide pamphlets in English, Chinese, Korean, and other languages, you should pick one up and read it carefully when using the subway.

Humans receive help from honeybees in producing vegetables such as tomatoes and pumpkins and fruits such as apples and melons. If people had to do this work themselves, it would require a great deal of labor. It would be completely impossible to do it in exactly the same way. default.p.III-1.vietnamese: Japan may be the country with more hot springs than any other. There are many wonderful hot springs throughout Japan, so many visitors from overseas come to Japan eager to experience them. An ordinary bath simply consists of heated water, whereas hot springs contain a variety of components that are beneficial to the body. The components vary from one hot spring to another. The etiquette for using a hot spring is similar to that for public bathhouses in towns. In many other countries, people enter hot springs wearing swimsuits, but in Japan, all clothing must be removed. In addition, before entering the hot-water bath, you should pour water over your body to remove dirt. This is an extremely important rule of etiquette so that the bathwater is not contaminated. You may take a towel into the washing area to scrub your body, but you must never put any object into the hot-water bath. This is also to keep the water clean. You should also lightly dry yourself before leaving so that you do not soak the floor of the changing room, where people remove and put on their clothes, by walking out while dripping wet. For this reason, many hot springs display information about their components and bathing etiquette. To prevent arguments caused by ignorance of the rules and to ensure that everyone can use the facilities comfortably, bathing instructions are provided in English, Chinese, Korean, and other languages. Since some Japanese people also do not know proper bathing etiquette, instructions are provided in Japanese as well. Apparently, in Hokkaido, where there are many Russian residents, signs are even written in Russian. I hope everyone will follow the rules of etiquette and enjoy hot springs to the fullest.

default.p.III-10.vietnamese:
As Japanese cuisine becomes more popular, increasing numbers of foreigners are coming to Japan to study cooking. Famous chefs are also coming to Japan. In fact, although Japanese cuisine is spreading around the world, many restaurants overseas serve such strange Japanese dishes that they cannot really be called Japanese food. This is because some chefs cook without any understanding of Japanese cuisine. If these strange versions of Japanese food continue to increase, it will cause problems. Therefore, it is extremely valuable that they come to Japan to learn about Japanese cuisine.

Recently, some chefs have begun using ingredients that create Japanese flavors, such as kombu seaweed (Note 1) and katsuobushi (Note 2), in dishes from their own countries. I was very surprised to hear that they had even started using them in French cuisine, whose flavors are completely different. I had thought they would not go well with Western food. However, I heard that French cuisine became even tastier by incorporating Japanese flavors. On the other hand, Japanese cuisine is also being influenced by foreign cuisines. Creative Japanese cuisine (Note 3) is currently very popular in Japan. Traditional Japanese cuisine generally does not use much oil or fat, but these creative dishes do not avoid ingredients commonly used in European cuisine. When we think about it, today many people travel around the world, so there are many opportunities to enjoy foreign food. It is only natural that delicious foods spread widely.

（Note 1）Kombu: A type of seaweed
（Note 2）Katsuobushi: Dried tuna shaved into thin flakes
（Note 3）Creative (sōsaku): Creating something new

default.p.III-2.vietnamese:
The expression “That person is sharp” was once used to describe someone who was intelligent, perceptive, or capable. Recently, however, it is often used negatively to mean, “That person loses their temper easily, so be careful.” In this context, “kireru” means suddenly becoming angry when faced with something unpleasant.

It is true that there have been more and more things lately that make people want to get angry. However, does nearly bumping into someone really warrant shouting at them so loudly? Even when the other person is apologizing, it is easy to notice adults continuing to yell loudly. Moreover, it is surprising that there are especially many elderly people among them. In the past, people often said that as people grew older, they became gentler and rarely got angry, but recently elderly people seem to be the opposite. Somehow, the number of elderly people who lose their temper at the slightest thing appears to be increasing.

In fact, people who are quick to anger are often said to be lonely or dissatisfied with something in their everyday lives. When they are already irritated and something goes against their wishes, even if it is only a trivial matter, the frustration they have accumulated over time explodes. The increasing tendency of elderly people to lose their tempers means that more elderly people are unhappy and that life has become increasingly difficult and suffocating for them.

default.p.III-3.vietnamese:
Since ancient times, Japanese people have believed in something called “kotodama” (the spirit of words), holding that spoken words possess a special power. Kotodama is the mysterious power believed to reside in words. In the past, people believed that whatever was said would become reality. For this reason, they disliked pronouncing the number “4” as “shi,” because it was associated with “death” (死, shi). This is why hospitals do not have a room number 4. Because people feared the power of words so much, certain expressions came to be avoided on occasions such as weddings and funerals. At weddings, words such as “break up,” “separate,” and “cut off” are not used. The same applies to wedding gift money: even numbers such as 20,000 yen are associated with “separation” or “parting,” so indivisible odd amounts such as 30,000 or 50,000 yen are preferred.

Because of this concern with words, Japanese people also enjoy wordplay. Of all its forms, they seem to particularly enjoy “goroawase,” or sound-based wordplay. Goroawase involves combining similar-sounding sounds. It is useful for remembering numbers such as historical dates and telephone numbers, so it remains widely used today. For example, 8783 can be read as “flower shop” (hanayasan), and 4192 as “beautiful country” (yoikuni). Consequently, desirable telephone numbers are even bought and sold. Eating tonkatsu before a match is another example, combining katsu in tonkatsu with katsu meaning “victory.” Recently, sashimi has also become popular among foreigners, but because sashimi can be interpreted as “pierced meat,” evoking the image of stabbing a body with a knife, high-end restaurants carefully avoid the word and call it otsukuri instead. Even if foreigners hear otsukuri, they probably will not know what it means. Today, people may no longer fully believe that words possess mystical power, but they still frequently change their wording to avoid making others uncomfortable.

(Note 1) Even numbers: numbers divisible by 2, such as 2, 4, and 6

(Note 2) Odd numbers: numbers not divisible by 2, such as 1, 3, and 5

Among my friends, there is one person who always thinks positively about everything. Once, we went on a road trip together. While heading toward a hot spring, we took a wrong turn and wasted about an hour. Yet she said: 「Thanks to taking the wrong road, we got to see such a beautiful view of Mount Fuji. We were so lucky!」. However, that was not the only road from which Mount Fuji could be seen so beautifully. From anywhere in the surrounding area, Mount Fuji looks beautiful. On the way home, we stopped at a rest area, where I forgot to turn off the car's headlights. When we returned after shopping and tried to start the car, the battery was dead and the car would not start. While we were panicking, the person in the Mercedes parked next to us asked what had happened. They quickly connected their battery to ours with the jumper cables they were carrying and helped restore our battery. When the car battery died, I was genuinely terrified and worried about what would happen. As soon as the car started again, my friend said: 「We really are lucky. Someone with jumper cables just happened to be parked right next to us」. How was that lucky? Normally, anyone would think it was an unusually unlucky event. We might not even have been able to get home that day. Yet even then, she still thought we were lucky.

Whether we consider ourselves lucky or unlucky depends on each person. But watching her, I felt that happiness seems to come to people who always believe they are lucky.

(Note) Battery: a rechargeable battery that can be used repeatedly.

default.p.III-5.vietnamese:
The format of stores changes with the times. Around 1950, stores were divided according to the goods they sold, with separate butcher shops, fish shops, and greengrocers. However, in the 1960s, supermarkets—where people could buy all their groceries in one place—became the central form of retail. Supermarkets then began selling clothing and household goods as well, steadily increasing their power and influence. By 1972, some supermarkets had sales exceeding those of department stores. However, pharmacies and liquor stores were protected by government regulations, allowing them to maintain their traditional format.

The era of supermarkets continued for a long time, but in the 1990s, convenience stores that stayed open late appeared. Although their prices were high, they became especially popular among young people. As a result, supermarket sales gradually declined. In addition, after regulations were relaxed and discount liquor stores opened, many traditional liquor stores went out of business or switched to operating convenience stores. During the same period, specialty retailers selling inexpensive electrical appliances increased their sales, while stationery stores went bankrupt because of the emergence of 100-yen shops selling inexpensive school supplies.

Today, convenience stores also sell inexpensive products. Moreover, large pharmacies have begun selling food as well. Some electrical-appliance stores even sell tissues and instant noodles. Since no one goes to an electrical-appliance store or pharmacy every day, these stores have started selling such items to attract customers.

How will the format of stores change in the future? I cannot imagine it, but I am sure that the current state of stores will not continue forever.

default.p.III-6.vietnamese:
Modern society is said to be busy, and the excessive amount of information makes people tired. In particular, when doing computer-based work, people use their brains rather than their bodies. The body recovers when it rests, but mental fatigue does not seem to disappear.

The best way to relieve mental fatigue is, of course, to sleep. In addition, spending time with animals, breathing in the fragrance of grass and trees in nature, and laughing and joking are also said to be effective. These activities calm the mind or put us in a cheerful mood.

When the brain becomes excessively tired, the brain itself is damaged. If that happens, the state of mental fatigue continues without end. Blood flow in the brain decreases, and the brain can no longer function effectively. This may be considered a medical condition.

To prevent this from happening, it is said that the brain contains a part that senses fatigue and sends out a warning signal. When you feel tired, you should rest immediately. Doing so allows the brain to recover. However, when we are doing something interesting, enjoyable, or beloved, our motivation to continue becomes stronger than our feeling of fatigue. As a result, we keep going without resting. Then, when the fatigue becomes excessive, even the part that signals fatigue stops functioning. Eventually, we become ill and need a long time to recover. Once we reach that state, medication may be necessary, but getting enough sleep is extremely important. Moreover, carrying out the activities mentioned above can also help us recover from the condition quickly.

default.p.III-7.vietnamese:
Among the objects that generate heat through the power of chemistry and are used in daily life is the「disposable body warmer」. It maintains warmth for about 10 hours without using a flame. It is commonly used when skiing, figure skating, or staying in cold places. A「disposable body warmer」is made mainly from fine iron powder. When iron comes into contact with oxygen in the air, it gives off heat. This phenomenon is called oxidation. The process is very simple. First, fine iron powder and other ingredients are put into a breathable pouch. The pouch is then placed inside an airtight bag. That is all there is to it. When the inner pouch is removed, the iron inside comes into contact with oxygen and gives off heat. Pots and kitchen knives are also made of iron, but they do not become hot when they come into contact with oxygen. This is apparently because the area in contact with the air is too small for them to heat up. However, since they are made of iron, they naturally still undergo oxidation. In other words, they rust. Rust is also a form of oxidation.

The「disposable body warmer」applies knowledge that anyone who has studied chemistry knows. Yet no one thought of using that knowledge to make a「disposable body warmer」. That is why everyone was surprised when it was put on the market. Once people learned how it was made, they said,「Is that all there is to it?」Even so, until then, no one had thought of making anything like it, although many people had had the opportunity.

The「disposable body warmer」has developed, and today the type that can be attached to clothing is the main product. This is because a type that can be attached anywhere is more convenient. The adhesive type was born from the feeling that the previous body warmers were inconvenient to use. I think this product was created from the basic desire underlying all inventions: the desire to make things more convenient.

default.p.III-8.vietnamese:
There are some very unusual companies in this world. They are companies that teach us「how to organize and tidy up」. They inspect areas of a company that are not properly organized and show employees how they should be arranged. Poor organization means spending a great deal of time looking for things. Even if the time wasted by one person is short, the total time wasted by all the employees can add up to a very large amount. For a company, that is a major loss. This is why companies specializing in organizing businesses have appeared.

At one company, employees were often troubled because they did not know where documents were. On one occasion, the company even lost a business opportunity because some paperwork could not be found. As a result, the director decided to ask an「organization company」for help. At first, the employees had no intention of cooperating with the organization company’s staff. However, after they moved the desks and filing cabinets as instructed, and sorted and reorganized the paperwork, their work efficiency visibly improved. In addition, strangely enough, work also began coming in more frequently. Needless to say, the employees were impressed and thereafter cooperated very enthusiastically.

What kind of psychology or way of thinking lies behind asking another company to organize one’s own company? I find it difficult to understand. However, apparently employees do not feel annoyed when advised by a specialist and are willing to follow the advice, whereas they may resent being reminded by someone within the company. As a result, the organizing process proceeds smoothly.

People say that young people are no longer very interested in getting married, but part of the reason is that they have fewer opportunities to meet potential partners. In the past, if someone did not have a partner, they would often be introduced to someone by relatives such as uncles and aunts, or by a supervisor at work. Today, as connections between people have become weaker, there are fewer people who can make such introductions.

Instead, matchmaking agencies have appeared. They have adopted various creative ideas to create opportunities for people to meet. Rather than simply holding parties where people eat and drink, they offer a wide range of activities, such as playing golf or cooking together.

Recently, matchmaking events at cafés with dogs or cats have attracted a great deal of attention. Since people who like dogs and cats gather together, they already have a topic in common. Furthermore, even if the conversation stops, they can simply play with the dogs or cats right in front of them, so there is no awkward feeling. As a result, participants do not feel as tense as they do at ordinary matchmaking events, and apparently they are still satisfied even if they do not get married because they had fun playing with the animals.

(Note) Konkatsu: activities undertaken with the aim of getting married.
